transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well, what brings me in is... I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next. It's like I can't just sit idle, you know? I'm always on the go. And recently, my job changed up our work setup, and it's just made that a lot harder to hide or manage.
Can you describe what you mean by always moving from one thing to the next? Do you find it hard to focus on one task for very long?

Yeah, I do find it hard to focus for very long. Like at work, if I'm in one of our longer coaching meetings, or... or when I'm reading a new procedure for customer service. I always start off fine, but after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes kept moving over the words, but I didn't really take in what was said or what I just read. I just kind of lose the thread of it without meaning to.
Do you find yourself acting impulsively or having trouble waiting your turn, like interrupting others when they’re speaking or blurting out answers before someone finishes a question?

Yeah, I do actually. I really don't mean to be rude, but... well, at work, if I hear my coworkers trying to figure out a customer problem, I'll just jump right in. I end up giving an answer before they've even finished talking, or before anyone actually asked me for help. I just sort of blurt it out without thinking.
Do these difficulties with focusing and acting impulsively happen in other places besides work, like at home or when you're with friends or family?

Yeah, it happens at home, too. Even with quiet stuff that's supposed to relax me. Like, if I try reading at home or sitting down to watch a movie with my wife, it doesn't last long. I'll start shifting around, making comments, or finding a reason to get up and do something else. I just can't seem to stay settled.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with focusing and staying still? Were they something you experienced as a child, or did they start more recently?

Well, looking back, this has been around long before this job change. It's definitely something I experienced as a kid. I remember back in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. They always noted that I talked out of turn and constantly had to be reminded to just stay with my work. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
When you were a child, did these difficulties with focusing and staying still happen in places other than school, like at home or with friends?

I'm not really sure about that. I mean, it's been a long time, and I mainly just remember what the teachers used to say on my report cards. I don't have a clear memory of how it was at home or with friends back then.
Can you recall if these difficulties with focusing and staying still were noticeable before you turned 12 years old?

Yeah, definitely. Like I mentioned a minute ago about my grade school report cards, that was well before I turned 12. So, yes, all that stuff the teachers wrote about me being careless and talking out of turn—that was happening back then. It's been around long before any of my recent jobs.
Do you often feel restless or as if you need to be constantly moving, even in situations where others typically remain still, like during meetings, meals, or quiet activities?

Yeah, I do. It's like... if I have to sit still through a training video at work, or if I'm stuck in a slow appointment somewhere, I start feeling kind of boxed in. I just get this strong urge where I feel like I need to stand up, stretch, or at least be doing something with my hands.
Do you find yourself forgetting daily tasks or getting easily distracted by things around you, even when you're trying to focus?

Yeah, I do. Especially with my job. I'll... well, I'll mean to call a customer back, or maybe answer an internal message right after my lunch break. But honestly, unless I write it down in more than one place, it can just completely slip my mind until the next day.
Have these difficulties with focus, restlessness, and forgetfulness caused you any significant problems in your job, relationships, or other important areas of life?

Yeah, they have. At work, it's actually started showing up in my performance reviews. My supervisors have been pointing out that I leave tickets unfinished, or I make careless mistakes that end up slowing the whole team down. It's frustrating because I'm really trying hard, and I generally get along great with the customers, but the focus issues are definitely causing problems there.
Can you recall if your difficulties with focusing and staying still were present in multiple settings during childhood, such as both at school and at home?

Yeah, they were. Looking back... well, this was around long before this job change. I remember in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I'd talk out of turn a lot, and they constantly had to remind me to just stay with my work.
As a child, did you feel overly active or restless at home, even when you weren't in school?

Honestly, I... I don't really remember that being much of an issue at home. I mean, my parents never really complained about me bouncing off the walls or anything. I was just a regular kid around the house, mostly just playing outside when I could. So, no, I wouldn't say I felt overly restless there, not that I can recall anyway.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or needing to move around even in situations outside of work, like at home or in social settings?

Yeah, I do. Even with quiet stuff that’s supposed to relax me, it happens. Like, if I'm trying to read at home or just sit through a movie with my wife... it doesn’t last long before I’m shifting around in my seat, making comments, or just finding an excuse to get up for something. I just have a hard time just sitting there and relaxing.
Do you notice these issues with staying focused and feeling restless in more than just work and home, like when you're out with friends, running errands, or in other social situations?

I don't really think so, no. When I'm out running errands or grabbing a bite with friends, I feel pretty normal. It's mostly just work and when I'm trying to relax at home that I notice it. I haven't really had any issues like that in other situations.
Can you recall if, as a child, you had trouble staying focused or sitting still during family meals or other quiet times at home, even if your parents didn’t mention it?

No, I really don't think so. I mean, thinking back to family dinners or just hanging around the house... I don't remember having any trouble sitting still or paying attention. I was pretty normal in that regard as a kid.
Do you find that these difficulties with focus and restlessness affect you in more than just work and home, such as in social situations or other parts of your life?

I think I mentioned this just a minute ago, but no, not really. It's pretty much just at my job and when I'm at home trying to relax. If I'm out socializing or doing other things, I don't really notice it being a problem. It really just seems limited to work and home.
Do you notice any difficulty focusing or feeling restless when you're in situations like public places, social events, or during errands, or does it only happen at work and home?
I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I said, no. It's really just work and home. When I'm out doing errands or at a social event, I'm fine. I don't have those issues anywhere else.
Can you recall if these difficulties with focusing or restlessness were noticeable in other settings during childhood, like during extracurricular activities, playdates, or family outings?

Well, looking back... I guess this has been around long before my recent job change. I don't remember much about playdates or things like that, but I do remember school. In grade school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. They said I talked out of turn a lot and always had to be reminded to just stay with my work. So, yeah, it was definitely noticeable there.
